title: Effectiveness of Generate–Validate–Repair (GVR) with Deterministic Validation vs LLM-only for Reducing Unsafe Network Changes
research_question: Does an automated generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses a deterministic network validator materially reduce the incidence of unsafe or semantically incorrect network changes relative to an LLM-only generation pipeline on a curated NetOps task bank?
confirmatory_hypotheses: A closed-loop generate–validate–repair pipeline incorporating a deterministic validator reduces the post-application unsafe-change incidence by at least 50% (relative reduction) compared to LLM-only generation on the same tasks (paired design).
exploratory_questions: What fraction of GVR-corrected cases introduce new, validator-undetected failure modes (GVR-introduced failures)?
How many repair iterations are required on average for successful repairs, and what is the average model-call cost per successful repair?
How sensitive are results to validator choice (primary validator vs independent secondary validator) and to task cluster (topology class)?
benchmark_scope: Curated public/synthetic NetOps task bank (200 confirmatory tasks) covering four topology clusters: enterprise, campus, datacenter, and edge (50 tasks each). Tasks are intent→configuration translation problems synthesised from public config corpora and canonicalized into machine-checkable intents.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API selected at execution time (deterministic sampling: temperature=0, fixed system prompt). Exact model identifier(s) will be recorded in execution manifest and disclosure.
Deterministic validators executed in Docker containers (primary: Batfish; secondary independent validator: data-plane emulator using Mininet + automated reachability test suite).
transformation_scope: Natural-language intent → device-configuration text outputs (Cisco-like IOS/JunOS snippets) with syntactic normalization to canonical representation for automated comparison and validation.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion of tasks that transition from unsafe under LLM-only to safe under GVR, reported as absolute and relative reduction; computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor using exact McNemar test).
secondary_estimands: Average repair iterations per repaired task (mean, 95% CI).
Proportion of tasks where GVR introduced a new validator-detected failure (GVR-introduced-failure rate).
Model-call cost per successful repair (mean, 95% CI).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: 200 tasks total (4 topology clusters × 50 tasks each). For each task: generate a single deterministic initial LLM output (one API call, stored). Paired conditions use the same initial output: (A) LLM-only — apply initial generated config to emulator/validator and record pass/fail; (B) GVR — run initial LLM output through deterministic validator; if validator reports violations, issue automated repair prompt to the same LLM (up to 3 repair iterations) and re-validate after each iteration; apply final repaired config to emulator and record pass/fail. Randomization: task ordering randomized for execution; seeds fixed for deterministic generation. Inclusion/exclusion: tasks with infrastructure execution failures are logged and handled per missingness plan.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 (registered analysis contract). Primary test: exact McNemar test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) on paired binary outcomes (LLM-only pass/fail vs GVR pass/fail). Report absolute risk reduction, relative reduction, and exact p-value; compute 95% confidence intervals for paired difference via exact/pivot methods supported by the executor. Secondary analyses: logistic regression (repair-success ~ topology_cluster + initial_validator_failure_type + repair_iterations) computed on confirmatory sample as exploratory analyses with multiplicity controls (see multiplicity_plan). Failed-call handling: use analysis executor's primary failed_call_treatment 'complete_pair_primary' (treat technical failures according to contract rules) and run sensitivity analysis using 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' to verify robustness. All inputs, seeds, model-call logs, validator diagnostics, and hashes will be recorded and published in execution manifest.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary confirmatory test (McNemar). All secondary tests are explicitly labeled exploratory. For post-hoc or multiple secondary comparisons, apply Bonferroni or Benjamini–Hochberg correction as appropriate; exploratory subgroup claims will be reported with unadjusted p-values but flagged as exploratory.
missingness_plan: Execution-infrastructure failures: pairs where neither condition completes are excluded from primary analysis and counted in a technical-failure log. Single-condition technical failures: follow paired_binary_analysis_v1 failed_call_treatment 'complete_pair_primary' (documented in execution manifest). Missingness is reported by task with deterministic exclusion/inclusion rules. No manual adjudication: all exclusion decisions are deterministic and logged.

benchmark_names: Public/synthetic NetOps task bank v1 (curated for this study)
risk_factors: Validator coverage blind spots leading to overfitting of repairs to validator rules (false sense of safety).
GVR introducing new failure modes not captured by primary validator.
Model API rate limits or outages causing incomplete pairs.
detection_procedures: Primary deterministic validator (Batfish) run on every generated/repaired config.
Secondary independent validator: Mininet data-plane emulator with automated reachability and functional test-suite run on a randomized 10% holdout of tasks (automated, deterministic).
Automated discrepancy detector: any task where Batfish and Mininet disagree on pass/fail is flagged.
Automatic logging of validator diagnostic messages and difference traces for every flagged item.
item_flagging_rules: Flag automatically if Batfish verdict != Mininet emulator verdict.
Flag if GVR completes with >1 repair iteration and final validator reports 'warning' diagnostics (non-pass states).
Flag if repair loop reaches max iterations (3) without a pass.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes tasks flagged for validator-emulator disagreement (predefined conservative treatment). Sensitivity analyses: (a) include flagged tasks as failures for GVR; (b) include flagged tasks as successes for GVR; (c) report results restricted to unflagged subset. All flagged-task handling is deterministic and automated.
residual_uncertainty: Residual blind spots where both deterministic validators agree but both miss a real operational failure that neither validator models.
External-validity gap between emulator-detectable failures and production-network failure modes.

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative (recommended) execution: single initial LLM call per task; expect low average repair iterations (≈0.3 repairs/task); run secondary validator on 10% holdout. Enforces strict model-call cap and per-task call caps to avoid rate-limit exposure.
models: hosted LLM API (single model; exact identifier recorded at execution)
transformations: repair prompts (expected avg 0.3 calls/task; max 3 calls/task when triggered)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Total planned_model_calls = initial_calls (200) + expected_repairs (≈60) + 10% overhead (40) = 300. This stays well under platform maximum planned_model_calls (10,000) and inside the estimated operational budget while preserving confirmatory sample size.

budget_scenarios.description: Generous budget: allows full worst-case repair iterations and expanded exploratory holdout testing and repeated repair-strategy variants.
models: hosted LLM API (single model; exact identifier recorded at execution)
transformations: up to 3 repair iterations per task (max worst-case budget)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case calls per task = 1 initial + 3 repairs = 4; for 200 tasks that is 800 calls. Extra headroom (3,000 planned) permits multiple repair-prompt variants, reruns for sensitivity exploration, and expanded exploratory discovery items while remaining within maximum_planned_model_calls (10,000).

power_plan.primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute and relative change in unsafe-change incidence between LLM-only and GVR).
power_plan.target_effect: 50% relative reduction in unsafe-change incidence (e.g., from 30% baseline failure rate to 15% after GVR); primary confirmatory target is relative ≥50% reduction.
power_plan.calculation_method: Exact McNemar test for paired binary outcomes (two-sided alpha=0.05). Power approximations use discordant-pair assumptions: with n=200 tasks, if baseline discordant pairs are consistent with baseline failure rate ≈30% and expected improvement yields discordant counts consistent with an absolute reduction of 0.15, power ≈0.8. Sensitivity analyses will report power under alternative baseline failure-rate assumptions (20%–40%).
assumptions: Baseline unsafe-change incidence (LLM-only) assumed in planning: 30% (uncertain — sensitivity analyses will consider 20% and 40%).
GVR effect hypothesised as a 50% relative reduction (absolute reduction 0.15 if baseline=0.30).
Pairs are independent across tasks (no cross-task contamination); dependence assessed in diagnostics and addressed if present.
Alpha=0.05 two-sided for primary test; power target=0.8 for planning.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With n=200 and the above baseline assumptions, the pre-registered minimum detectable absolute reduction is approximately 0.12–0.16 depending on discordant-pair distribution; sensitivity analyses will report exact detectable-effect curves.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power and main test under baseline failure-rate assumptions 0.20 and 0.40.
Run primary analysis restricted to unflagged tasks (no validator-emulator disagreement) and report effect sizes.
Perform the failed-call sensitivity analysis per registered analysis contract.

transformation_families: Syntactic canonicalization (normalize device/line order, whitespace, canonical interface names).
Semantic parsing to canonical rule objects (ACL entries, route statements) for equivalence checks.
Repair-prompt-derived deltas applied to canonical representation; re-serialization to device config text for validation.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Automated parser validates that generated/repaired config implements the intent-specified invariants (reachability/blacklist invariants represented as canonical checks).
Compare canonical rule objects before and after repair to detect unintended semantic changes beyond target fixes.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject repaired config automatically (label as failure) if repair introduces any rule that contradicts the declared intent invariants or introduces deny/permit changes outside repair scope.
Reject if repair loop reaches max iterations (3) without a validator pass; mark as unresolved.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated holdout audit: 10% of confirmatory tasks (randomly selected with fixed seed) are executed on the secondary validator/emulator (Mininet) to detect validator overfitting; all audit outcomes are logged and trigger automatic flags if disagreement occurs.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Mapping from intent to canonical representations is unit-tested with a small deterministic suite of canonical intent→config examples included in the repo; all mapping checks run automatically in CI prior to the main run.
residual_risks: Parser bugs causing incorrect canonicalization (mitigated by unit tests but residual risk remains).
Semantic constructs outside validator/emulator modelling (e.g., vendor-specific features not modelled by Batfish or Mininet).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulator and validator fidelity vs production networks (external validity): results are explicitly scoped to the curated public/synthetic task bank and emulator/validator models used.
Exact hosted LLM model identifier(s) and runtime characteristics (latency/cost) will be recorded only at execution time; availability risk is mitigated by per-scenario call caps and enforcement.
Validator coverage blind spots: secondary validator and holdout audits reduce but do not eliminate unmodelled failure modes.
